literal_meaning: একটি পেটে এবং আরেকটি মুখে (one in the belly and another in the mouth)
figurative_meaning_en: Duplicity or hypocrisy (saying one thing inwardly and another outwardly)
similar_in_english: Say one thing and do another
example_sentences_in_bangla: সে পেটে এক মুখে আরেক, কখনো তার কথায় বিশ্বাস করা যায় না।
রাজনীতিতে অনেকে পেটে এক মুখে আরেক হয়ে থাকে।
example_sentences_in_english: He is two-faced; you can never trust what he says.
Many politicians are duplicitous, saying one thing in public and thinking another.
note: This idiom reflects traditional Bengali views on sincerity and trust in social interactions.
